question: The rate law for this reaction CO (g) + NO2 (g) --> CO2 (g) + NO (g) is rate = k[NO2]². Which one of the following could be a plausible mechanism for the reaction?
options:
A. NO2 (g) + NO2 (g) --> NO3 (g) + NO (g) [slow]

NO3 (g) + CO (g) --> NO2 (g) + CO2 (g) [fast]

B. NO2 (g) + NO2 (g) --> NO3 (g) + NO (g) [fast]

NO3 (g) + CO (g) NO2 (g) + CO2 (g) [slow]

C. NO2 (g) + CO (g) --> NO (g) + CO2 (g) [slow]

NO (g) + CO2 (g) --> NO2 (g) + CO (g) [fast]

D. NO2 (g) + NO (g) --> NO3 (g) + NO2 (g) [slow]

 NO3 (g) + CO (g) --> NO2 (g) + CO2 (g) [fast]

question: Which one of the following COULD NOT be considered as factor influencing the rate of chemical reaction?
options: The rate constant of the reaction
explanation: The rate constant (k) is a parameter that quantifies the rate of a reaction at a given temperature; it is not an external factor that can be changed directly. Temperature, catalysts, and surface area of reactants are factors that influence the rate by affecting collisions and activation energy.

question: In which of the following order of a reaction, a plot of ln[A]t versus time is a straight line whose slope is -k?
explanation:
For a first-order reaction, the integrated rate law is ln[A]t = ln[A]₀ - kt. Plotting ln[A]t versus time gives a straight line with a slope of -k.

 Zero-order reactions give [A]t versus time as straight lines, and second- and third-order reactions follow different integrated rate laws.
